Hi Emily / Jake —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the clear context on the clinical-guidelines use case. Short recap + our recommended next steps so we can lock the pilot scope.

Recap (notes from our side):
- Goal: support clinician-facing Q&A and guideline retrieval (summaries + citations) with minimal hallucination risk.
- Corpus: mixed PDFs and markdown-backed policy docs (you estimated ~450k docs; please confirm sample export).
- Constraints: compliance/audit logs required, prefer VPC/private deployment, p95 latency target for end-to-end retrieval+generation < 750ms if possible.
- Success signals: recall on grounding docs, grounding precision (percent of model answers citing correct doc), low hallucination rate.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Share recommended model stack + prompt sets and an offline eval plan (we've attached a short sample prompts CSV and a scope doc).
2) Synapse to confirm corpus size and provide a 200-document sample + 200 representative queries by 2026-10-12.
3) Redwood to run offline RAG eval (recall@k, MRR, grounding precision, latency) and return benchmark report by 2026-10-15.
4) If metrics look good, run a 2-week pilot (private/dedicated) with live traffic expected 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-30.

Quick recommendations (high level):
- Embeddings: dense embeddings (SBERT variant) + hybrid sparse signals for clinical terminology.
- Retriever: approximate nearest neighbors with an initial top_k=100, re-rank top_n=10.
- Reranker: cross-encoder style reranker for precision (we'll propose a small-footprint variant to keep latency down).
- Generator: instruction-tuned model with citation-aware prompting; incorporate source attribution tokens.

I've attached: Synapse_Scope_Doc.pdf (scope / compliance asks) and sample-prompts.csv (initial prompt set).

Can you confirm the corpus sample timeline and whether the VPC/dedicated pilot is required for legal review? Once we have that, Marissa will share a short eval plan and target metrics to validate fit.

Cheers,

Karthik / Grace — adding a more technical set of recommendations we can present to Synapse. Copying Emily for transparency.

Proposed eval & stack (initial):
- Embeddings: sbert-large-msmarco (or equivalent) for dense vectors; supplement with a clinical sparse vectorizer (BM25 with clinical stopword list).
- Indexing: FAISS HNSW for ~450k docs (good latency / memory tradeoff). Use IVF+PQ only if we need more aggressive compression for Dedicated nodes.
- Retriever pipeline: dense ANN -> top_k=100 -> sparse scoring merge -> rerank top_n=10.
- Reranker: cross-encoder (bert-base-msmarco-cross) tuned for precision. If 10k+ QPS required, fallback to a lightweight dual-encoder + calibration layer.
- Generator: redwood-instruct-4o (8k context) with citation-anchored prompting. We'll prepare prompt templates that explicitly ask for source-lined answers and a 'confidence' score.

Evaluation plan (offline):
- Query set: 500 representative queries (we'll ask Synapse for 200 and sample 300 from our benchmark of similar clinical tasks).
- Metrics: recall@10, recall@100, MRR@10, grounding precision (manual label: whether the top-cited doc actually supports the answer), hallucination rate (manual annotation), and p95 latency for retrieval and reranking steps.
- Acceptance thresholds (initial): recall@10 >= 85%, grounding precision >= 90%, hallucination rate <= 5%, end-to-end p95 <= 750ms. We can iterate thresholds after first offline run.

Compliance notes:
- For PHI redaction we recommend running a pre-ingest redaction + storing vectors inside Synapse's VPC (we can support private deployment connector).
- Audit logs: we can surface per-request document IDs and reranker scores to an S3/Cloud logs sink; legal can consume that for audits.

Operational notes:
- Reranker latency: expect ~20-80ms per item for a cross-encoder on a dedicated GPU instance; re-ranking top_n=10 usually adds ~150-300ms end-to-end depending on instance type. We'll include latency vs accuracy curves in the report so Synapse can pick their tradeoff.
